- owns: `platform/folders/<id>`, `platform/memberof/<sub>/<manifest:unit.rows>/<id>`, `platform/memberof-gone/<sub>/<manifest:unit.rows>/<id>`;
- reads: `domain/folders-state`, `platform/manifest/<sub>`, `<sub>/<manifest:unit.rows>/<id>`, `domain/grants`.
- `name`: there is no uniqueness among siblings.
- `members`: a unit can stand in several folders.
- `folders`: there is no empty list — the membership row is removed.
The folder id does not repeat: the console chooses it itself, the caller does not set it.

The membership key is longer than the unit key by the 18 bytes of the prefix `platform/memberof/`.\nTherefore a unit whose key `platform/memberof/<ref>` does not pass the key rules of P/01.1 N1 (the limit of 1024 bytes) is never\na member: `400 bad member`. The key cannot be shortened (chapter 6.1 N3 «Full keys and store refusal»).
Rows of tables are never members. This way the platform does not know the kinds of subsystems, and a subsystem has one answer to the question of what lies in a folder.

Only the batch holds the link invariant: no write of the chapter changes one side without the other, except for two windows: a unit\ndeleted past the door — the unit's side is already dead; and a non-live folder that the batch removed from `memberof(U)` (N3 «folder rows in a batch» step 6) — the folder is not visible. The reaper removes both links (N3 «folder reaper»).
- A new folder has no descendants, and its parent is older than it and set forever. Therefore a cycle cannot exist.
- Depth is at most `FOLDERS_DEPTH_MAX`.

- The tombstone row is not removed: the version of its index is needed by the feed\n  ([chapter 6.1](06.1-console.norms.md) N2 «Change feed»), and the `id` does not repeat, so there is no one to resurrect the folder or to occupy its key anew.

- **A write over a folder tombstone is a refusal.** The rule of [chapter 6.1](06.1-console.norms.md) N3 «create» step 8 on a write over a tombstone does not apply to the family\n  `platform/folders`: a resurrected folder would bring back a subtree that is already deleted as seen from outside.
- Only a live folder is given out by the read doors. An unreachable row does not exist from outside until the reaper removes it.
- In a cluster in a domain, `members` of a folder row are only units of this cluster: `GET /folders` shows its own ones, a member has no full member list.
- The key `platform/memberof-gone/<ref>` is longer by 5 bytes: the limit of N1.1 is counted by it.

Every actually mandatory deletion request (target, done and other claim/auxiliary requests, separately) fits the store's actual entity-body ceiling B inclusively: compact JSON, UTF-8, required escaping, every metadata field and delimiter, plus the actual final LF.

The counted serialization has comma and colon separators without spaces, non-ASCII characters as UTF-8 bytes rather than `\u` escapes, no NaN or Infinity, no BOM, and no LF other than an actually sent one; every actual LF adds one byte. HTTP framing is excluded.

All full keys, CAS/index/id/deadline strings/numbers, membership/gone rows, complete prepared unit/claim rows and guards are counted; auxiliary internal rows have no exemption from this ceiling. A FOLDERS_PER_UNIT_MAX*FOLDER_ROW_MAX items sum does not prove this obligation.

B is actual Status.max_body, V is actual Status.max_value, F is FOLDER_ROW_MAX; no default is substituted. H bounds all encoded metadata after removing put items; each put is assigned once to a proved unit/tombstone, claim, three-field folder or empty-map category. Full finite metadata/multiplicity proofs give, for each packet:\n\n`H + (n_unit+n_claim)*(12*V+7) + n_folder*(6*F+19) + 2*n_empty + LF <= B`.
The 12V+7 bound counts worst string escaping and every field, 6F+19 uses the folder's three fields; H includes deletes, all guards and framing inside the JSON entity.
In the finite deletion profile, every other nonempty auxiliary family is counted by an explicit proved weight category.

The admission or refusal of the profile is not per-mutation admission, a new DELETE refusal or a dynamic bypass. A conservative profile can require a much larger B than the store default declared by its -max-body form row; item weights alone cannot make deletion available. Existing caller batch refusals remain refusals of the whole batch, not a substitute for the static deletion obligation.

Check the complete decoded list of `platform/folders` and `platform/memberof` before a procedure uses it. A list beyond its limit makes the whole row unreadable and follows the existing family outcome; no prefix is accepted and no list is shortened. This applies to the reads of R013, R014, R016 and R018. No separate rule for an older state applies.
The segment `folders` is closed by the loader to the names of subsystems, units and tables ([P/02.1](../../02-installer/spec/02.1-installer.norms.md) N1.2a).
References to all members are given to the holder of the grant without a filter by the `view` of the units: otherwise `index`\nwould change from edits that the reader does not see.
`POST` has no field `members`: the member list is set by `PUT`.
At the folder doors another method — `405 method`.
At the folder doors a path longer than `/folders/<id>` — `404 no such path`.
A folder has no `revision`: a number, like any other value, — `400 If-Match is a unit revision` before\nthe row is read.

The index has diverged — `412 folder moved`, the body `{detail, error, field: "/index", row: Folder}`: `row` — the current row; when there is no row, for a tombstone and without `view`, there is no such field.
At the folder doors `done` of the claim goes as a write of the batch, as at `POST /console/batch`.
The reference of `?member=` is the full key of the unit, percent-encoded; not by the form — `400 bad member` without `field`.
- `guards[]`: the row of each added member if it is not in `writes`.
In the batch door, `delete` of a folder row — `400 bad batch`: only the folder door deletes a folder. The order of the checks — N3 «folder rows in a batch».
The store batch of a write of this chapter is an internal batch of the console: it is limited by weight, not by\n`BATCH_WRITES` (chapter 6.1 N1.4).
The chain, the rights, the fingerprint and the claim are read before the batch; a break before the batch leaves nothing.
A listing failure of `GET /folders` — `503 unavailable`, not\nan empty list.
In `PUT` of a folder the body sets the order of the members.
The batch of a folder deletion does not touch subfolders: from this index they are unreachable, the reaper removes their rows and membership.
- A removal requires the right to `U`, because an exclusion of the role `none` at the folder tier could forbid `U`: the removal would raise the rights.

- At a removal the right to `U` is judged in the subsystem of the unit: a row `none` of another `sub` is removed by this same right, this is a policy. The reason is the same as for adding: a right in one subsystem does not\n  become a right in all of them.
- Adding to a folder is a person's will, therefore it goes by the right to write the folder, also in a batch with the creation of a unit.
At a unit deletion by the door the version of the folder changes together with the member list, because the folder row is written by the same batch.
There is no second writer of the family: the controller does not write rows `platform/*`.

The rows of «unit deletion by the door» that the console puts into the batch are not counted in the caller's `BATCH_WRITES` and do not enter the caller's incoming body; they fully count in the serialized entity of the emitted store request and its static profile bound (N1.3).

An explicit folder body that still contains a deleted U, or an explicit memberof put that restores its membership, is `400 no membership`, with `field: /writes/<n>/key` of that conflicting explicit row, before any target data write. Do not rewrite the caller's body silently. The existing response memory remains in effect.

An explicit folder without U and an explicit memberof delete are consistent; a missing memberof delete is supplied by the ordinary deletion procedure. Reuse each consistent explicit key once and add only missing automatic consequences.
In this reconciliation, rights exemptions apply only to automatically added consequences, while explicit rows keep their ordinary rights checks.
The reconciliation does not list all folders or replace the existing unknown/unreadable-memberof procedure.

Step 4 of the folder reaper still reconstructs from the full member lists, with the existing writer-form check: it neither truncates the reconstruction nor permits an out-of-form write. There is no special transition for an older state.

- An edit of the member list against the deletion of a unit, the edit first: the deletion batch carries `cas` or a guard of the absence of the membership row. The new membership refuses the batch, the procedure re-reads the row and removes the unit from the new folder too.
- Creating a subfolder against the deletion of the parent: the parent's guard. The folder does not appear under a deleted branch.
